subject: Observability wiring & SIEM bridge for Polaris VPC deployment
messages:
From: Alice Nguyen <alice@polaris-cloud.com>
To: rafael.mendes@redwood.com
Cc: security@polaris-cloud.com
Date: Sun, 1 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Observability for VPC build — SIEM/trace hooks questions

Hi Rafael,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. We're starting to draft our telemetry handoff checklist for the Polaris private VPC deployment and I need to clarify a few things before we sign the onboarding SOW:

- Which delivery mechanisms does Redwood support for private deployments? We prefer HEC over syslog but can accommodate either.
- Do you provide an IP allowlist and short-lived tokens or do we need to manage an intermediary forwarder?
- We have strict PII egress rules — can Redwood perform scrubbing (PII masking) before telemetry leaves our VPC, or do you require that to happen upstream?
- For traces: what format do your tracehooks expect (OTLP or a simple JSON envelope)? Any sample payloads you can share would help.

Attaching our initial SIEM schema so you can map fields. Can you loop in whoever will own the runbook + evidence requirements on your side?

Thanks,
Alice Nguyen
Head of Platform Security
Polaris Cloud

Attachment: polaris-siem-mapping.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: rafael.mendes@redwood.com <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice@polaris-cloud.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 1 Aug 2027 12:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Observability for VPC build — SIEM/trace hooks questions

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear checklist. Looping in Kimberly (Infrastructure) and Marissa (Solutions) to scope the mapping and runbook. High level answers below and a recommended next step.

- Supported transports: HEC (HTTPS POST with token) and syslog over TLS. HEC is preferred for structured events; syslog is an option for legacy appliances.
- Authentication & network: Preferred pattern is an allowlisted egress IP range + short-lived HEC tokens generated by our private connector. We can optionally place a forwarder inside your subnet if you require zero egress.
- PII scrubbing: Redwood can apply configurable scrubbing rules in the forwarder that runs inside your VPC (recommended when you have strict policy). We do not by default ship raw PII offsite.
- Traces: we accept OTLP over gRPC and a lightweight JSON tracehook for small event sets. See attached tracehook-spec for examples.

Proposed next step: Marissa, can you propose a minimal acceptance checklist (HEC token demo, sample log ingestion, and tracehook example) and a 2-week timeline for initial acceptance?

Rafael
Account Executive — Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice@polaris-cloud.com>, rafael.mendes@redwood.com
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 2 Aug 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Observability for VPC build — SIEM/trace hooks questions

Hi Alice, Rafael —

I've attached a concise tracehook spec and a short HEC vs syslog decision matrix to help your ops team. Summary of the technical choices we recommend for Polaris (VPC):

1) Primary path: Splunk HEC (HTTPS) into a dedicated ingestion token + IP allowlist. Token rotation endpoint documented in the runbook.
2) Alternate: syslog-tls to an internal forwarder, then forwarder -> Redwood HEC for canonicalization. Use this if you cannot allow direct egress from app subnets.
3) Scrubbing: run the Redwood forwarder (container) in your telemetry subnet. It runs configurable scrub rules (regex, redaction, field removal) and samples before sending. We can provide a default PII rule-set; your compliance team must sign off.
4) Traces: we support OTLP gRPC for full traces (recommended), and a JSON lightweight hook for heartbeat-style traces. JSON hooks expect the envelope: {"service":"...","span_id":"...","trace_id":"...","attributes":{...}} — examples in tracehook-spec.md.

Acceptance checklist (draft):
- Polaris can POST to HEC token endpoint from test forwarder.
- Sample logs ingested and mapped to Polaris SIEM schema (3 event types).
- Trace sample shows 95th p99 latency < 200ms from collector to Redwood ingestion in our staging test.
- PII scrub rules applied and verified against the spreadsheet mappings.

Proposed timeline:
Week 1: deploy test forwarder in Polaris staging subnet, exchange tokens, ingest samples.
Week 2: run load/PII verification, finalize runbook and schedule evidence handback.

Attachments: tracehook-spec.md, polaris-siem-mapping.xlsx (updated)

--
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Alice Nguyen <alice@polaris-cloud.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, rafael.mendes@redwood.com
Cc: security@polaris-cloud.com, eng@logstitch.io
Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2027 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Observability for VPC build — SIEM/trace hooks questions

Marissa, Rafael — this is great, thanks. Quick clarifications from our side:

- Polaris will provide an HEC endpoint that accepts tokens (we prefer token-based auth). We'll schedule the token rotation window with you.
- Our SIEM team prefers canonical JSON over syslog where possible. We'll plan for HEC first.
- PII scrubbing: Polaris policy requires scrubbing to occur inside the customer network. We'll run your forwarder/container in our telemetry subnet and ask Redwood to provide the default rule-set for review.
- Evidence: we need an auditable proof of custody for 90 days (delivery receipts + checksums) and a signed statement of handling from Redwood for the production rollout.

I've looped in our SIEM integrator (eng@logstitch.io) to confirm field mappings; they will validate the attached spreadsheet and return comments by EOD Friday.

Next steps: can we lock a runbook review meeting Wednesday next week (Aug 11) at 10am PT?

Regards,
Alice

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: rafael.mendes@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: Alice Nguyen <alice@polaris-cloud.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Aug 2027 15:30:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Observability for VPC build — SIEM/trace hooks questions

Team — quick security note and proposed owner assignments before the runbook review: 

- Encryption & custody: we'll require TLS 1.2+ for HEC and recommend mTLS for the forwarder-to-Redwood control channel. Evidence (delivery receipts + SHA256 of batched files) will be captured and stored in the customer's evidence bucket for 90 days. Legal will prepare a handling statement template.
- Scrubbing: because Polaris requires in-network scrubbing, Redwood will provide the forwarder container with the default PII ruleset. Compliance (Polaris) must sign acceptance; we will not change rules without a documented change control.
- Roles:
  - Runbook owner: Marissa Cole (Solutions) — leads acceptance checklist and test sign-off.
  - Network & infra: Kimberly Park — coordinates allowlist, private connector placement, and perf targets.
  - Security & evidence: Hannah Schmitt — owns the evidence collection spec + proof-of-delivery format.

Action items before the Aug 11 meeting:
1) Marissa: publish the short runbook (drive link above) and sample ingestion curl commands.
2) Kimberly: confirm whether Polaris needs an internal forwarder (syslog) or can allow HEC egress from the telemetry subnet.
3) Rafael: lock the Aug 11 runbook review and invite Legal if Polaris requests a handling statement pre-signature.

I'll draft the evidence spec and attach to the runbook by Monday EOD.

-Hannah
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
